approved: True-up Shortfall Levy (Excise) (Carbon Tax Repeal) Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that repeals the carbon tax and introduces new rules to prevent price exploitation.

The package would prohibit businesses from failing to pass on cost savings from the carbon tax repeal for key goods like electricity and gas, with penalties of up to 6,471 penalty units ($1,100,070) for a corporation.
Electricity and natural gas retailers and bulk synthetic greenhouse gas importers would have to provide statements to the ACCC estimating cost savings passed on to customers.
Prohibits price exploitation by requiring affected entities to pass through all cost savings from the carbon tax repeal.
Introduces new ACCC powers to monitor prices and issue substantiation notices to retailers and importers.
Requires electricity and natural gas retailers to prepare and communicate a statement to customers about estimated cost savings for the 2014-15 financial year.
Businesses that supply electricity, natural gas, or bulk synthetic greenhouse gases, and their customers.

Moved a debate management motion to fast-track passage of the carbon tax repeal bills through the House together, arguing the September 2013 election gave the coalition a clear mandate, and recalled the 2010 pledge that there would be no carbon tax under a government Julia Gillard led.

Moved the second reading of the carbon tax repeal bills, saying Treasury modelling shows households will save an average of $550 a year, that the tax has cost $15 billion over two years, and citing an Independent Competition and Regulatory Commission estimate that electricity prices in the ACT will fall by 11.6 per cent once it is repealed.
True-up Shortfall Levy (Excise) (Carbon Tax Repeal) Act 2014
